title: Quick check: Creating Your First React Project

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Creating Your First React Project”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Understanding available project starters should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Understanding available project starters should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Creating Your First React Project: Understanding available project starters should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Understanding available project starters?
options: Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Creating Your First React Project: Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Creating Your First React Project” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Creating Your First React Project: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
